text:
I need to verify whether Pittsburgh was indeed named after a British Prime Minister.

Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania was named after William Pitt the Elder (also known as William Pitt, 1st Earl of Chatham), who was British Prime Minister from 1766-1768 (and effectively led the government during the Seven Years' War in the 1750s-60s). The city was named in 1758 by General John Forbes after the British captured Fort Duquesne from the French.

The other agents are correct in identifying Pittsburgh as the answer. This is a well-documented historical fact.

Answer: Pittsburgh
